systems.name: creative-apps
systems.description: The macOS app shells of the creative suite: five SwiftUI apps (Flare, Design, Photo, Library, Halo), each over a Linux-safe Model target, plus the SuiteUI design system.

containers.name: SuiteUI
containers.description: The shared design system (Sources/SuiteUI): tokens, Liquid Glass primitives, the SuiteWindow shell, toolbar palette, sidebar rows and sections, content-layer surfaces, pro inspector rows and scrub fields, a thumbnail grid, a timeline strip and AppMark, the app marks. macOS only; knows no app Model or engine, only SuiteModel's app list.

components.name: SuiteUI sources
components.description: The shared design system (Sources/SuiteUI, linking SuiteModel for SuiteApp): spacing, radius, size, type and color tokens; Liquid Glass applied in one snapshot-aware place (Glass) and GlassPanel; the SuiteWindow shell (sidebar, content, inspector) with SidebarSection and SidebarRow; ToolbarGroup palette actions; the content layer (CanvasSurface, SurfaceCard, EmptyStateView, ViewerStatusBar, BusyNote for open, save and import progress, and TransportCapsule, the shared transport over TransportStepping); the editor-kernel chrome (SuiteExportSheet, SuiteStrokePacer, SuitePointerPressure, BrushCursorMark, and ToolKeys, the one tool-letter lookup and the one map from AppKit modifier flags to KeyModifiers); the editor shell after the Ripple editor (EditorShell, EditorTopBar and its bar items, the docked ToolbarGroup rail, CanvasViewport with its Ruler, optional checkerboard, ZoomMath clamped zoom and fit with SuiteCanvasNavigating, the live CanvasNavigating over it, SuiteHandleGeometry, the live HandleGeometryProviding over the kernel's BoxMath and HandleHit, and CanvasMarks with SelectionHandlesEditor, the selection box whose handles resize and rotate it, SegmentedTabs and the ColorWell hex row, with the eyedropper's EyedropperButton, SampleLoupe and SampleSizeChips); pro inspector parts (InspectorHeader, InspectorRows, ScrubField and NumericInput number entry); the Studio easing parts (CurveEditor, StudioScrubRow, ChoiceChips); ShapeToolOptions, the shape tool's kind chips and per-kind rows with their range help; AppMark, the one view that draws an app's mark (icon, glyph or line style) from AppMarkArt, path data scripts/render-marks generates from Bundle/Marks; ThumbnailGrid with its selection math; HistoryPanel, the one History panel over the kernel's HistoryListing, and the autosaveRecovery modifier over SuiteModel's RecoveryFolder (autosave-history); StrokeEditor, the one stroke editor, which sends the kernel's StrokeIntents and never edits a document (stroke-style); and TimelineStrip with its frame mapping, shared by Flare and Halo, with TimelineLaneLayers, the rules of its AppKit lanes renderer (which lanes redraw from an Equatable diff, a layer frame per lane, a press routed to the lane classification); MenuCommand, the one menu item, built from a SuiteKernel CommandSpec (MenuCommand+Catalog) so its title, enabled state and why-not help come from the app's command catalog; SuiteGallery, the component gallery the journeys drive, with a command-catalog page over the kernel's FakeCanvasDocument; and PathEditOverlay with PenTool, the Pen and point editor's overlay (a placeholder drawing the path only, on a local contour stand-in until the kernel's path types land). HistogramView (a ToneHistogram's bins in the field well with shadow and highlight clipping markers), shared by Library's develop panel and Photo's Levels. UnsavedGuard is the one unsaved-changes asker: the unsavedChangesGuard modifier and UnsavedGuard.proceed show the kernel's UnsavedPrompt as a Save, Don't Save or Cancel sheet before a dirty window closes, its document is replaced or the app quits (adopt-kernel-unsaved-prompt). FontPicker is the one font picker (font-picker): a search that ignores case and accents, the family list drawn in each family's own face, the Face menu and the Size row, over FontPickerRules (filter, face order, nearest face) and the FontPicking contract; the gallery page runs on FakeText's families or a host's live list.

containers.name: FlareApp
containers.description: The Flare app (2D animation): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/FlareApp, built from SuiteUI. Reads FlareModel and calls its methods; never writes its state (scripts/ci app-state rule).

components.name: FlareApp sources
components.description: The Flare app (2D animation): the SwiftUI App scene, its menu bar (FlareCommands) and views in Sources/FlareApp, including the inspector's TIMING row (FlareInspectorTiming: the selected span's easing preset name) and the easing popover it opens (FlareEasingPopover: presets, the four bezier numbers and the curve) on the live FlareWorkspace, built from SuiteUI, and PlaybackDriver, which feeds NSScreen display-link target timestamps into the workspace's play clock, and StagePath, which turns FlareCore paths and colors into CGPath (one addCurve per cubic) and sRGB CGColor for the stage, and StageRasterizer, the PNG export rasterizer (LA-1): FrameRasterizing on a CoreGraphics RGBA8 sRGB bitmap that draws a StageDrawList at 1x or 2x exactly as the stage does, the background unless transparent, and encodes it through ImageIO, and FlareAutosave, which writes the dirty document's RecoveryFile atomically off the main actor once autosave is due and removes it after a save, and on launch reads and decodes it off the main thread into a RecoveryOffer to restore or discard, and FlareWindow, the SuiteWindow with the toolbar, sidebar and inspector that routes every control through one FlareIntent, and FlareToolItems (each FlareTool's palette title, symbol and one-key shortcut), the router (FlareWindow+Router and one FlareWindow+<area> file per FlareIntent area, each acting or giving the reason it can't), and the window's area views: FlareStage (the artboard drawn in a Canvas on CanvasViewport, its overlay of draft, marquee and selection outline drawn from the drag's FlareLiveDrag while one lasts, so the window's body runs once per drag, the floating tool palette, the rulers the View menu toggles, the hidden zoom readout, and FlareStageGuides, the ruler guides pulled out of the rulers, moved and dropped back on them), FlareTimeline (one TimelineStrip lane per layer, ruler scrub and the timecode and frame readouts), FlareTransport (start, step, play/pause, end and loop; FlareCanvas runs PlaybackDriver while playing and the stage status bar shows the rate pills), FlareRecording (the auto-key recording ring), FlareFilePanels (the open, save and export folder panels, the title's dirty dot, and the save and open alerts), FlareExportSheetAdapter (the Model's export run on SuiteUI's export sheet under flare.export ids, with FlareExportOptionRows in its options slot: the frame, step, scale and background rows, the warnings, the file count and the problem line; FlareWindow+Export runs the exporter off the main actor and writes its files all or nothing, never over an existing file), FlareInspector (Properties and Library tabs), FlarePasteboard (Cut, Copy and Paste carry the Model's layer bytes on NSPasteboard.general under the suite's SuiteTypeID.flareLayers, and a change-count watch keeps Edit > Paste current), FlareStageContextMenu (the stage's Cut, Copy, Duplicate, Delete, Bring Forward and Send Backward, each disabled with its reason) and the stubs later tasks fill (FlareLibraryPanel and the new sheet, open status and recovery modifiers).

containers.name: FlareModel
containers.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Flare's window. FlareWorkspace: the open FlareCore document, selected scene and drawing tool. FlareHeadless: the same document with no window for the CLI (open, save, SVG and Lottie export). Foundation only, value types.

components.name: FlareModel sources
components.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Flare's window: FlareWorkspace (document, selection, tool, frame and playback, drafts) and FlareServices: the use-case contracts, their live conformances over FlareCore (LiveStage, LiveHits, LiveShapes, LiveProperties, LiveKeyframes, LiveEasing, LiveScenes, and LiveExportAdapter, FlareCore's SVG, Lottie and PNG exporters over any stage: text removed first, a cancel between PNG frames writes nothing, every result carries ExportScan's warnings), and the fixture fakes the UI track and snapshots run on. FlareLaunch parses the launch flags (-FlareFixture, -FlareSample, -FlareOpenFile, -FlareSaveTo) into the workspace's first document and services, and FlareServicesBuilt is FlareServices.built, the live type for every member whose live conformance has merged, which a launch without -FlareFixture runs on. FlareIntent names every control of the window as one case per area with a stable identifier, and FlareIntent+Titles gives each its menu or toolbar title. FlareStageRead gives the stage its draw list (the drag preview while a move runs) and marks (draft, marquee, selection bounds); FlareTimelineRead gives the timeline its rows, empty text and selected row; FlarePenFinish ends an open pen path on Return as one step. FlareWorkspaceState holds the export, assist and file-load states the workspace stores. FlareFiles opens .flare files through load (progress first, a pure decode the app runs off the main thread, then the landing), hands the app a save's bytes, and keeps the file name, the window title and the dirty flag (the document against the one last opened or saved), with section 3.3's alert text for each FormatError, the Open Recent list (file paths, most recent first, at most ten), and the autosave due time (30 seconds after the last edit, only while dirty) with the recovery bytes of the dirty document, and restoring a recovered document as unsaved, untitled work; FlareFiles+Kernel reads the dirty flag and the autosave verdict from SuiteKernel's DocumentSession, ends every coalescing run on a save, and gives the launch offer as the kernel's RecoveryOffer. FlareSelection picks layers or items by click, Shift-click and marquee, and gives the selection box's bounds; FlareDrag turns stage gestures into a draft or move preview and commits each once, on mouse-up, as one named undo step; FlareLiveDrag runs a drag's samples on a copy of the workspace the window doesn't observe, for the stage to draw until mouse-up hands the window the last one; FlareDrawing adds the Ellipse tool's draft and its one-step commit; FlareScenes adds, renames, removes (never the last), reorders and sets up scenes; FlareGuides adds, moves (one coalesced step per drag), removes and clears ruler guides, and FlareGuideDrag is one guide drag on the stage, shown as it moves and turned into one step's view intents on release; FlareEdit runs the Edit menu (Cut, Copy, Paste, Duplicate, Delete, Select All, Deselect), each one named undo step or disabled with the reason it refuses with; FlareAnimate holds auto-key and the inspector's animated properties (Mixed across layers, one coalesced step per scrub, the stopwatch and keyframe button); EasingEditing is the easing editor's contract, which FlareWorkspace conforms to over FlareCore's SetKeyframeEasing, with FakeEasingEditing as its in-memory stand-in for UI work. FlareOnionState holds onion skin and motion path preferences and reads ghosts and the path from services.onion. FlareServices holds one fake per use-case contract (FakeScenes, FakeStage, FakeHits, FakeShapes, FakeProperties with section 2's not-animated rule, FakeKeyframes, FakeEasing, FakeOnion, FakeLibrary, FakeMachines, FakePreview and FakeExport with FakeRasterizer so far, NotBuilt for the rest) over the fixture documents in FlareFixtures (empty, bounce, character, button, button with states, button with machine and showcase). ExportScan names everything an export can't write (text, symbol animation, machines, Lottie's background); FlareExport holds the export sheet's options, warnings and run. FlareSymbols holds the Library tab's symbols and swatches, Convert to Symbol, place, the reason Delete is disabled while a symbol is in use, and editing a symbol in place: the owner switch, the symbol's length on the timeline and the scene frame to return to. FlarePlaybackTicks is the playback driver's platform-neutral core: PlaybackTicker turns display-link target timestamps into the elapsed seconds the play clock advances by, FlareWorkspace.tick is the link's entry point, and PlaybackBudget holds QB-L4's dropped-frame gate. MachineLayout lays out a state machine's graph for the Interactions editor: columns by breadth-first distance from the initial state, unreachable states in a last column. FlareMachines holds the Interactions editor's state: the edited machine, states from frame labels, transitions and inputs, each edit one named undo step through services.machines with refusals in machineError, and the live preview over services.preview, which any machine edit stops. BoxGestureMath is the box move, scale and rotate math FakeShapes and LiveShapes share; its handles 0...7 are SuiteKernel's EditorHandle ring, numbered and placed by the kernel through BoxGestureMath+Kernel. FlareLayers+Kernel projects the edited owner's layers into SuiteKernel's LayerTree (FlareLayerPayload), whose front-to-back order and rows the Layers section reads, and runs each panel move through LayerTree.move before FlareCore's ReorderLayer. EasingEditing+Kernel and KeyframeEditing+Kernel put Flare's easing presets, curve, keys (.all for the summary key) and key and frame rules on SuiteKernel's Keys (EasePreset, EaseCurve, KeyRef, Segment, KeyRules). FlareFill+Kernel makes FlareWorkspace SuiteKernel's GradientFillTarget: the first painted shape's fill in its bounds, the no-shape help, and runFill, which sends a gradient editor gesture through the catalog with a refusal in paintError (the set is a stub until gradient-fill FG-5). FlareDocumentCommands+Catalog gives every FlareCore command id in CommandRegistry.builtIn a SuiteKernel catalog spec over FlareWorkspace (kebab-case id, SchemaProbe's schema or a hand-written one for layer commands, available when its example runs on a copy, run through the engine as one undo step, read back by FlareCoreHistory), with CommandSchemaProviding schemas for FlareCore's payload enums. FlareCommandCatalog adds the app's commands (file, edit, object, tool, animate and scenes ids, each available exactly when the window's control is, with its menu title) and builds FlareWorkspace.catalog from both lists.

containers.name: DesignModel
containers.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Design's window: pages, the node tree on each page (with fills and text) and which Layers rows are expanded, the selection, the tool, the model-owned undo history, the canvas gestures and the file codec. Foundation only, value types.

components.name: DesignModel sources
components.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Design's window: DesignWorkspace (pages, the selected page and node, the tool, the open file's URL), the multi-layer selection (DesignSelection: the ordered selected layers with the last as primary, Shift-click toggling, the box around them), DesignNode (the node tree on a page, each node with a fill and text, in absolute page points) and the tree flattened into rows under the expanded set, DesignHistory (the model-owned undo and redo, one named step per edit; New File's step carries the replaced document's file URL, which Undo puts back), the canvas gestures (hit testing, the handles a selection shows, draw, move, resize, nudge, delete, in DesignCanvasEditing and DesignDrawing), what the canvas shows before a click (DesignCanvasHints: the hover answer, the Text tool's placement box, the size badge and where it hangs), what an arrow, Delete, Escape or Return pressed on the canvas does, ignoring the numeric-pad flag every arrow carries (DesignCanvasKeys), the inline text edit, whose commit fits the box to the measured text in the same step (DesignText), where the canvas puts a frame's name, above the frame or inside it at the artboard's top (DesignFrameLabel), the inspector's header lines (DesignInspectorContent), the lock that covers a node's subtree and the line saying why (DesignLocking), the Layers row's eye and lock toggles, the hidden-in-tree check and the move target a drop above, below or into a row maps to and the insertion line a pointer over a row draws (DesignLayerToggles), the held-id index id minting reads (DesignHeldIDs), aligning the selected layer to its enclosing frame or page with the reason a command is off (DesignAlign), the window toolbar's eight commands with their titles, symbols, identifiers and the reason each can't run (DesignToolbarItems), the page's size as one undo step, its visible content bounds and which layers reach past its edge (DesignPageSize), the file codec (DesignFile), the open document as SuiteKernel's DocumentSession over the history's step serials, a save setting its saved token and ending the edit run, and the file version read through VersionedJSON.probe (DesignSession+Kernel), the export contract (DesignExport+Kernel: the scope and options, the workspace's export targets, plan and SVG readouts over the export slot, and the remembered options, never a history step), what the export sheet reads (DesignExportSheet+Kernel: the scope chips' titles, the options it opens with, a whole 1x to 3x scale, the run's shown options and the file list with skipped hidden layers) and the SVG text of nodes inside a box (Live/DesignSVG), what a PNG of a planned export item draws (DesignRaster: the item's nodes moved to the origin on a page its whole-point size, the plan's pixel size and scale, a side over its max refused), the eyedropper's sample adapter onto SuiteKernel's SampleTarget (DesignSample+Kernel: why nothing can be sampled, the colour of the topmost visible painted layer at a point, and applying it to the selection's fill or stroke as one step), the stroke adapter (DesignStroke+Kernel: a node's stroke as the kernel's VectorStroke, the workspace as SuiteKernel's StrokeTarget with its help, trim refused in Design, and the stroke editor's intents as the inspector's style change), the loupe the eyedropper shows at the pointer and a click's pick (DesignLoupe: the pointer's page point, the colour read there and whether Option sends it to the stroke), the layer tree adapter onto SuiteKernel's LayerTree (DesignNode+Kernel: a node as the kernel's layer payload and back; Live/LiveOrdering's Move Layer and Arrange, Live/LiveGrouping's Group and Ungroup, Live/LiveDuplicating's Duplicate, the Layers rows and the lock cascade run on it, and the refusals map to Design's by layer name), and the use cases a workspace runs on (DesignServices, whose `.live` set is NotBuilt in every slot until each feature lands: each help says the feature isn't built yet and each write refuses; `.fake` is the fixture fakes in Fakes/ that snapshots and fake-mode journeys use), and the workspace actions the window, menus and canvas call (DesignActions: each command's help and run through the services as one named undo step, one-layer delete, nudge and align on today's methods, Zoom to Selection and Select All; DesignActions+Edit: Copy, Cut and Paste, with Paste into the selected frame, Move Layer, and the inspector's style rows as DesignStyleChange, one-layer frame, fill and corner radius on today's methods), the command catalog (DesignCommandCatalog: every DesignCommand, palette tool, page and file action as a SuiteKernel CommandSpec whose availability is today's help and whose run is today's method, under ids kept in Tests/command-ids/design.txt), what the menu bar's items read (DesignMenuState: those specs over the focused window's workspace, with the menus' own rules for Open, a focused field's Undo and Redo, Rename Page and Align), Design's document with no window for the CLI and the real jobs (DesignHeadless: open and save through the file codec, the catalog lifted onto the workspace, SVG export of every page's top-level frames), and DesignLiveEdit: the copy a canvas drag or inspector scrub shows until it ends, then replays into the workspace as one step, and the gradient fill (DesignFill+Kernel: a node's kernel Fill in its unit box, the workspace as SuiteKernel's GradientFillTarget, and runFill, which sends a fill gesture through the catalog).

containers.name: PhotoApp
containers.description: The Photo app (raster editing): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/PhotoApp, built from SuiteUI. Reads PhotoModel and calls its methods; never writes its state (scripts/ci app-state rule).

components.name: PhotoApp sources
components.description: The Photo app (raster editing): the SwiftUI App scene and views in Sources/PhotoApp, built from SuiteUI's SuiteWindow: the window and its intents, the window toolbar (Open, Save and Export beside the title, Undo, Redo and zoom trailing) with the save status as its subtitle, the layer list in the sidebar, the canvas under a floating tool palette with the status line beneath it, the inspector (an image header over an Adjust | History tab switch: Adjust holds tool options, the selected layer's blend settings, and adjustment sections with the Levels gamma ScrubField and the Curves tone curve over its histogram; History is SuiteUI's HistoryPanel, which a row click jumps through and Window > History opens), the export, image size and straighten sheets (the straighten preview turns the canvas picture on the GPU under a grid), the File, Edit (Undo, Redo, and Cut, Copy and Paste on the image unless a text field has focus or a sheet is up), Select, Image, Layer and View menus, the general pasteboard read and written as PNG and TIFF (PhotoPasteboard) and watched for the Edit menu, the coalescing canvas renderer, the stroke pacer that applies a display frame's drag samples at once, the pen pressure and the Option key read from AppKit for canvas drags, the window's autosave to a recovery file and its restore offer at launch (PhotoAutosave), the app delegate (Finder opens, and the unsaved-changes prompt on Quit) and the window's close guard that asks before a dirty window closes, and the ImageIO codec behind PhotoModel's PhotoImageCodec.

containers.name: PhotoModel
containers.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Photo's window: the canvas as a CoreRaster PixelBuffer, its layer stack, selected layer and tool, adjustment settings, and inspector and Layer menu state; the free transform's handle hit and drag math adapt onto SuiteKernel (LiveTransform+Kernel); the canvas picture renders through CoreRender's dispatcher on a PhotoRenderRoute. Foundation only, value types.

components.name: PhotoModel sources
components.description: Linux-safe state and logic behind Photo's window, each menu, toolbar and palette action also a SuiteKernel catalog command (PhotoCommandCatalog: ids, availability from today's help, menu labels; PhotoMenuState, the spec each menu item is built from, with the menu's window, sheet, text focus and pasteboard), PhotoHeadless (the window-less document the CLI and real jobs drive: open .ora, PNG and JPEG, save .ora, export PNG or JPEG at an optional long side, the catalog lifted onto it) over CoreRasterImageCodec (PNG and JPEG through creative-core, with a small own 8-bit PNG reader and writer until core's lands):PhotoWorkspace (the open image's size and name, the layer stack with each layer's offset and its pixels as copy-on-write CoreRaster tiles (TiledPixels), so an edit copies only the tiles it touches, the selected layer, tool, and the brush's and eraser's own tool options with the brush cursor diameter, the marquee selection and pending crop), the tools' drags (brush and eraser strokes and clone dabs sampled through SuiteKernel's stroke model, StrokeSmoother and DabSpacer, with each tool's options kept as kernel BrushSettings and a list of BrushPresets; marquee, crop, move, and the Clone and Heal tools' Option-click to sample and drag to clone or heal), the clone stamp (a sampled source and a stroke that copies from it at a fixed offset onto the selected layer, and heal, the same stroke with each dab shifted to the tone where it lands), selection edits and crop, Image Size, Rotate and Straighten (worked out off the main actor, committed unless the image changed), the undo history (the tiles an edit changed, layer lists and whole stacks, read as a list of named steps from "New Image" or "Open" with a jump to any step), the tile-parallel renderer with damage tracking (a full frame as the reference, or the live canvas's update: only the damaged tiles, premultiplied), and on the GPU the live route (adjustments and adjustment layers as CoreRender tone programs over a cached composite of the pixel layers, written to the canvas texture in one pass) and the adjustments it applies (exposure, levels, curves, hue/saturation, blur) with the curve editor's samples and histogram, opening and exporting through the PhotoImageCodec protocol, the adjustment settings and logarithmic gamma track (with the Gamma field's commit, a no-op for the value it shows), what the inspector shows (with the image header lines and the viewer status size text), and when each Layer menu item can run (with Bring Forward and Send Backward, one place up or down the stack, and Select Layer Above and Below), the layer stack's reorder, arrange, duplicate and show/hide run on SuiteKernel's LayerTree (a single-level tree of PhotoLayer payloads, bottom first, projected to and from the top-first list), and the live edit services (the clipboard and layer merging, through the renderer's per-layer composite) behind Cut, Copy and Paste of pixels (a pasted layer, or a new image with none open) and Duplicate Layer, Merge Down and Flatten Image, each one named undo step with its reason when it can't run, and the eyedropper as SuiteKernel's SampleTarget (PhotoSample+Kernel: its sample size, the composite's colour at a point, a pick into the brush colour as tool state), and Free Transform, the layer flips and Canvas Size as SuiteKernel's TransformTarget (PhotoTransform+Kernel: the draft's or layer's box, begin, commit and cancel).

components.technology: Swift 6, Foundation (FoundationEssentials), CoreRender and CoreRaster; CoreRenderMetal and Metal on macOS

components.name: Retouch
components.description: Retouch/: the paint bucket and the heal tools over creative-core. BucketOptions (tolerance 0 to 255, contiguous, all layers, anti-alias) and BucketRules (the seed's flood mask times the selection's coverage, the colour mixed in by it), HealRules (spot heal and remove through filledFromSurroundings, heal through healed from a source offset, and a stroke's DabCoverage grid placed into a buffer-sized mask), and RetouchCommands, the four edits a raster app adds on a RetouchTarget: fill.bucket, retouch.spot-heal, retouch.heal and retouch.remove, one undo step each. Photo adopts them through PhotoWorkspace's RetouchTarget conformance (PhotoModel/PhotoRetouch+Kernel.swift; its old per-dab tone-match heal is gone). Library's dust-spot fix is the next adopter: a conformance of its develop target to RetouchTarget, calling retouch.spot-heal.

containers.name: afterglow CLI
containers.description: The headless `afterglow` command line tool: drives every app's command catalog on files with no window (`afterglow <app> <command> --json '{…}'`, open, export, list-commands, describe) and runs `*.jobs.json` scripts over sets of input files, which are also the real-jobs suites. One JSON object on stdout per run, sysexits exit codes. AfterGlowCLICore holds the router and every route, testable in process; AfterGlowCLI is the thin executable (product `afterglow`). Builds and runs on Linux, so cloud leads and CI drive the apps through it (docs/blueprints/suite/features/afterglow-cli.md).

components.name: CLI runner
components.description: The `afterglow` executable (AfterGlowCLI/main.swift: hands the arguments and LiveIO, the real disk with stdout and stderr, to CLI.run and exits with its code; CLIBinaryTests spawns it to check it agrees with CLI.run in process) and the router in AfterGlowCLICore: CLI.run, CLI.version and the sysexits codes (CLI.Exit), with the parser, output, file system and app registry files the single-shot forms use. CLIIO is everything the CLI touches outside itself (files, globs, stdout, stderr), with FakeIO, the tests' in-memory file system, and LiveIO, the real one (regular files only, a 2 GiB read cap, writes that make missing folders, then land a temp file by rename or by a hard link that refuses an existing target, globs walked without a shell); Apps is the registry, each app's HeadlessDocument erased to a HeadlessApp (photo, design, flare, halo, library, plus the fake for tests) whose HeadlessSession runs, saves and exports one open document. CL-1 makes `--version` live (one JSON object, sorted keys, exit 0); every other form exits 69 naming the slice that builds it until CL-4 fills them.

components.name: CLI batch runner
components.description: `afterglow run <script.jobs.json>`: ScriptRunner, which runs a versioned list of command steps over a set of input files and writes each output by name template, and Script, the format's Codable shape and validation. CL-7 fills it over the catalog's runBatch: validate the whole script (version 1, a known app, every step id and the output format), expand the inputs in sorted order, plan every output and refuse collisions (73) before anything is written, run each input all or none when atomic, and print one report; files are reached only through CLIIO.

components.name: Real-jobs harness
components.description: RealJobs: runs a `Tests/RealJobs/<app>/<job>/` script through the batch runner (ScriptRunner, its report captured) and compares each expected output: sha256 on the whole digest (a pure-Swift SHA-256, FIPS 180-4), JSON parsed and compared equal, or pixels within a tolerance in 255ths. A job whose platforms leave this one out is skipped before it runs with "macOS-only: <why>"; a pixel expectation is skipped "waits on image-codecs" until creative-core can decode PNG, never passed. Prints one JSON report: ok, or the failing paths and why, or skipped and its reason.

components.name: MCP server
components.description: `afterglow mcp`: a Model Context Protocol server over stdio that serves every app's command catalog as tools. MCPVersions pins the protocol revisions (2026-07-28 sessionless; 2025-11-25 and 2025-06-18 start with initialize); JSONRPC frames one JSON-RPC 2.0 message per line; MCPServer (with MCPOptions: apps, roots, limits) answers each line; MCPTools lists the tools and routes a tool name to an MCPRoute; MCPSessions holds the open documents by expiring handle and returns MCPToolResults. MC-4 builds the server: strict JSON-RPC parsing (-32700, -32600), version negotiation (-32602 listing supportedVersions), server/discover, initialize, ping, tools/list, rate-limited tools/call, silent notifications, and serve (`--app`, `--root`, `--live`) reading stdin line by line. MC-6 builds the tools: each app's open and new, then afterglow.save, export and close, then every command as <app>.<id> in id order with input {doc, params} and annotations from its kind. MC-8 builds the calls: open and new give a UUID handle and the summary ({doc, summary}), each command runs through the app's catalog ({result, undoStep?}), save and export write {path} only under the roots and never replace a file without force, close drops a handle; paths are checked by their real location (.. folded, every symlink resolved, the roots' own included); at most maxOpen handles, each expiring once idle for idleSeconds; why-nots, schema issues (each /path: message), refused paths and dead handles are tool errors (isError). MC-11 builds `--live` (macOS; refused with 69 elsewhere): LiveBridge finds the running apps' sockets (<app>-<pid>.sock under Application Support/AfterGlow/live), asks each for live/describe over LiveWire (newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 on a same-user Unix socket, UnixSocketLink), lists their commands as live.<app>.<id> with input {params}, skips a dead or garbled socket, and forwards each call as live/run with the client's name from initialize; an app's needsGrant answer (-32010) is the tool error "<App> asked you to approve this client", any other refusal the app's own words.
